Bird Brain

A flock of angry birds teaches itself to fly through obstacles using neuroevolution. No datasets, no backpropagation. Only survivors pass on their synaptic weights.

4x
Generation 1 is running with 120 random neural brains.
Who is learning fastest?
Scarlet (4-4-1) Ash (4-8-1) Rust (4-16-1)
Best score (obstacles cleared) reached by each species, generation by generation.
  1. Spawn random brains120 birds across three neural architectures with randomized weights.
  2. Everyone fliesEach bird reads 4 inputs (altitude, distance, gaps) every frame and decides: flap or wait.
  3. Survivors breedThe furthest-flying birds pass their synaptic weights to the next generation via crossover.
  4. Mutate and repeatSubtle Gaussian mutations (yellow highlights) discover optimal aerodynamic policies.

Reading the networks: Green connections denote positive weights, red is negative, thicker lines indicate stronger influence, and yellow pulses highlight recent mutations.
Keyboard shortcuts: Space / Click Flap (Human Mode) or Pause, H Play vs AI, N Next Gen, R Restart, M Sound, ↑/↓ Speed, C Record Mode.
